##  · K5-q-ties — R12 ties: order among several equal-pass wakers; what counts as a wake

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 3

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

Evidence: Clarifies R12's wake-first rule. Later wakers rank ahead of equal-pass queued budgets (LIFO; no starvation, since the pass advances). Simultaneous wakes are reconciled once per kernel entry under an explicit rank rule over kernel-assigned budget ids. A slice-end requeue goes FIFO behind equals. A wake is zero runnable threads to at least one. The tie counters' overflow is addressed; mutations R12TieQueuedFirst and R12RequeueAhead plus a tie boot case. It goes into the K5 KERNEL-SPEC docs commit; the owner confirms at plan approval.

### K5 implementer · Question

Event: `958d342eed0c71e9b38bea769ee0f114` · 2026-09-24T17:52:34Z

> R12: "a waking budget is ranked ahead of already-queued budgets with an equal pass". Three orders are open:
> (1) Two budgets wake at different times, both at the same pass. Literally the later one is ahead, since the earlier one was already queued when it woke, which makes wakers LIFO.
> (2) Several budgets become runnable in the same kernel entry. One IRQ plus timeouts expiring together is an example.
> (3) Where does a budget descheduled at slice end with threads still runnable go among equals? It isn't waking.
> 
> Recommendation:
> - (1) Literal: a later wake ranks ahead of earlier queued equals (tie key: wakes take a decreasing counter).
> - (2) Wakes are reconciled once per kernel entry (once per model op), in ascending budget id.
> - (3) A requeue goes FIFO behind equals (tie key: an increasing counter), so a descheduled budget can't win its own tie.
> - A "wake" is a budget going from zero runnable threads to at least one. Another thread of an already-queued budget becoming runnable doesn't move it.
> 
> All of this is deterministic and mirrored in the model, with mutations R12TieQueuedFirst and R12RequeueAhead.
> 
> Ask: approve, or give the order.

### Orchestrator · Answer

Event: `8ac677af6c7128ebcff0eb27b1231ac0` · 2026-09-24T17:53:52Z

> Approved, with two precisions:
> - (1) Literal LIFO among wakers with equal passes. Fine: the pass still advances when a budget runs, so an earlier waker is next once the later one has been charged. It can't starve.
> - (2) One reconcile per kernel entry, or per model op, is right. State the resulting RANK, not just the processing order: with a decreasing wake counter, processing in ascending id puts the highest id first. Pick the rank you intend, write it as a rank rule, and check that budget ids are kernel-assigned, so no process can choose an id to win simultaneous ties. Say so in the plan.
> - (3) FIFO behind equals for a slice-end requeue: approved.
> - "Wake" means zero runnable threads to at least one: approved. Another thread of an already-queued budget becoming runnable doesn't move it.
> - Tie keys: say how the counters behave on overflow, or why they can't overflow (u64 on both widths?).
> Mutations R12TieQueuedFirst and R12RequeueAhead: approved. Include a boot case for the tie rule, since it's a WP-K5 acceptance line. The three clarifications (I13, current minimum, ties) go into one KERNEL-SPEC docs commit. The owner sees them at plan approval.
